findings.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Recheck the non-development cache after acquiring the write lock, otherwise every concurrent initial cache miss serially reloads and overwrites it.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Queued cold-cache callers never recheck the cache after acquiring the exclusive lock, so each serially rereads and reparses the full manifest, multiplying startup work and latency.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No concurrent cold-cache test asserts that only the first non-development caller loads the manifest, so the missing cache recheck after lock acquisition is undetected.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — Queued cold-cache callers never recheck the cache after acquiring the exclusive lock, so each serially rereads and reparses the full manifest, multiplying startup work and latency.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, after acquiring the exclusive lock at line 48, the code does not recheck if entryPointAssetsCache has been populated by another goroutine that held the lock first. The pattern shown is: RLock -> check cache -> RUnlock -> Lock -> proceed without rechecking. This means if multiple goroutines find the cache empty simultaneously, they all queue for the exclusive lock, and each one will serially reread/reparse the manifest instead of rechecking the cache after acquiring the lock. This is a classic double-checked locking bug that causes unnecessary redundant work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — No concurrent cold-cache test asserts that only the first non-development caller loads the manifest, so the missing cache recheck after lock acquisition is undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real bug in the diff. After acquiring the write lock at line 45, the code does not recheck if entryPointAssetsCache is still nil before proceeding to load the manifest. This is a classic double-checked locking bug: multiple goroutines could pass the initial RLock check (when cache is nil), then each would acquire the Lock sequentially and redundantly load the manifest. The fix should recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock. This is a correctness issue in concurrent code.
